newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: MOTOR RACING-PROTESTERS DUMP OIL ON GRAND PRIX TRACK.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-PROTESTERS DUMP OIL ON GRAND PRIX TRACK.

text.p: Australian Formula One Grand Prix officials mounted a clean-up operation on Friday after protesters dumped diesel fuel on the track in an apparent protest about the site used for the race.
The fuel was dumped along a 500 metre stretch on the pit straight of the Albert Park street circuit, the venue for the opening race of the 1997 Formula One season on March 9, organisers said.
Protesters have waged a lengthy campaign to stop the race from being staged in a parkland area near the Melbourne's city centre.
Victorian premier Jeff Kennett described the incident on Thursday night as appalling and irresponsible.

"Many see this act of bastardry -- and that's the only way you can describe it -- as criminal. It's unforgiveable," said Kennett, who helped persuade Formula One bosses to switch the grand prix from its previous home in Adelaide last year.

Race chief Ron Walker told reporters: "I can assure all Australians that the race will go ahead on time, on schedule, and it will be one of Australia's greatest sporting events despite this vandalism."
A fire brigade official said the fuel might have to be burned off the road surface if detergents failed to solve the problem.
Police said the action was a deliberate attempt to disrupt preparations for the Grand Prix festival, which starts next Thursday and involves the closure of several public roads.
A spokeswoman for the Save Albert Park protest group denied responsibility.
"I'm dismayed because I think the lunatic fringe could let it rebound on us," spokeswoman Diana Burleigh said.
